general_information.Description: This course helps students to answer three important questions: what is public relations, why we do it, and how we do it? The course also introduces students to the tools and techniques they will need to carry out the role of public relations practitioner. More importantly, it introduces and examines the steps in the public relations planning process, which is central to the study and practice of public. Lecturer will use several teaching methods such as conducting group discussion and sharing field work experiences in the market on top of regular teaching. Students will have the chance to present their work as well as their thinking process related to this firm.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend more than 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/gui/Home for up-to-date course information

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand the history, basic concepts, principles of effective public relations, and the main theories of public relations across the business, government and not-for-profit sectors
Develop and execute a public relations campaign that responds to the need of the organization, using appropriate tools, tactics and writing skills.
Enhance the skills to communicate effectively to different audiences
Identify, analyse and evaluate strategic public relations campaigns across a wide range of media and communication disciplines
Evaluate how team roles and processes contribute to team performance
Identify how to act ethically and professionally, and be accountable when conducting a professional communication campaign

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Test the acquainted knowledge which student obtained in the delivered chapters 1, 2, 3, 4 5, 6, 7 and 8.
assessments.Grading Guide: Type: Individual Report Length: 3,000 words including references or indented quotes Task Description: The critical essay is intended to help students identify basic concepts and principles of effective public relations by analysing a key development, change or issue applied to the field of PR and professional communication. Students will choose a topic, from the list provided, or they may provide a detailed topic of their own to be cleared in writing by the lecturer. The topics are intended to justify some of the themes covered in the course and provide them with the opportunity to gain their knowledge and examine how their topic impacts on society, publics, consumers and professional practice. Notes: Students should provide clear illustrations/examples in their essay to show their understanding of the topic. All topics are written as a draft. Lecturers have the privilege to change the content of each topic as much as they want. Choose one from the following essay topics: Topic 1: Examine Public Relations best practices for going viral and generating UGC (User-generated content) Research and critically analyse the use of the words “viral” and “UGC” in this context, providing illustrations and academic support for your argument. Topic 2: Examine the differences between Advertising campaign and Public Relations campaign. Additionally, in your analysis consider whether Public Relations has been driven by the Advertising industry. Topic 3: Examine the role of Public Relations in social change Research and critically analyse the use of the words “social change” in this context, providing illustrations and academic support for your argument. Topic 4: Students may write their own topic accepted by their lecturer. It must be at a level ‘equal’ to the topics provided. Note: Students must not submit an essay on an alternative topic that has not been cleared.
assessments.Note: The essay topics should be updated or different at least 30% to the previous ones.

assessments.Grading Guide: Participation grade will be given based on students' attendance, students' attitude, preparation, contribution of discussions

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Test the acquainted knowledge which student obtained in the class.
assessments.Grading Guide: Type: Group Project Including: Written Report/ Proposal + Presentation Task Description: Students assume they are working for a public relations agency and responsible for creating a public relations campaign, which must include a realistic strategy for a real-life organization’s product, service or NGO issue/cause. Students will design, develop and evaluate a campaign for a “real” client. They will meet the client face-to-face, take a brief and be tasked with developing industry-ready materials for a public relations campaign. Or students will be provided with a list of current issues, and organisations linked to or impacted by those issues. From the list, they will select one issue and one organization to take care of. Or Students can make an event for a NGO (Combo 2) A campaign proposal for the client must include at least: (1) Executive Summary (2) Situation Analysis (3) Target Audience and key stakeholders (4) Goal (5) Objectives (6) Key Messages (7) Strategies and Tactics Including communication tools: electronic/interactive media kit (ex: news releases, photographs, glossaries, fact sheets, FAQs, executive profiles, videos), brochures, digital media platforms (ex: blogs, social media, newsletter, magazine, etc.); print (posters, fliers, etc.), events and other promotional materials and elements (8) Risk Analysis (9) Budget (10) Evaluation Execution phase can be PR materials, event... Notes: Students should illustrate excellent knowledge of public relations theories and how they can be applied. Critical skills in planning and execution of a public relations campaign also must be showed. To broaden the knowledge of various PR functions, students may choose one of the dimensions of PR activities: corporate PR, branding PR activities, personal PR, etc.
assessments.Note: The mark will be given based on each student's performance, not on the whole group's. It means each student will get their own mark.
